content.title: Explainer Kit: From Personal Workflow to Public Lifecycle Product
content.description: A final engineering recap of the boundaries, architecture, revision, and acceptance evidence that made Explainer Kit ready to ship.

sections.title: Original Request
sections.prose: The work began with a proven personal explainer workflow that could not safely serve as a public contract. The goal was to extract a reusable engine and an OAT lifecycle bridge while leaving personal destinations and orchestration in private wrappers.

sections.title: Key Agent Decisions
sections.prose: The implementation keeps configuration and destinations outside the core, requires one explicit author for unattended runs, and treats curated styles as the supported visual entry point. It also distinguishes normalized-object identity from retained-byte integrity and makes publishing additive so unrelated objects are never removed.

sections.title: As Built Architecture
sections.prose: OAT binds approved lifecycle artifacts and resolves public configuration into one versioned request. The core reconciles those sources with a critic, invokes a structured author, renders the selected recipe and style, runs content and browser quality gates, and records manifests, immutable hashes, and optional durability evidence.

sections.title: Implementation Record
sections.prose: Five delivery phases established contracts, the rendering pipeline, lifecycle integration, publishing, and release acceptance. A post-merge revision then closed the first-consumer gaps: full recap-package hashing, authored unattended content, four hand-designed styles, normalized Codex TOML output, and end-to-end adapter coverage.

sections.title: Validation Evidence
sections.prose: The finished branch passed repository checks, package builds, lockstep release validation, and a 65-measurement browser matrix. Packaged Stoa Wave 6 acceptance verified authored narrative, all retained immutable bytes, archive export, and unchanged source material; the final narrowed review reported no findings.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.prose: Explainer Kit now ships as a public core plus OAT adapter, with private wrappers remaining external. The reconciled branch targets public package version 0.2.11, records explainer-kit 1.0.2 and oat-explainer-kit 1.0.1, and carries the completed documentation and acceptance evidence in PR 170.
